title: Opposite post-processing orders of fermionic horizon channels and their quantum-resource monotonicity
abstract: Relativistic quantum-information studies in noninertial and black-hole settings often determine resource behavior through explicit calculations for particular input states and state functionals, leaving unclear whether the recurring monotonic trends originate from those choices or from a common underlying structure. In this work, we formulate the effective single-mode fermionic horizon transformation as a pair of complementary exterior and interior quantum channels, corresponding respectively to the physically accessible and inaccessible sectors, and establish exact post-processing orders in opposite directions. As the relativistic channel parameter $q$ increases, the exterior channel becomes progressively degraded, whereas the interior channel is ordered in the reverse direction. These relations extend to arbitrary multipartite settings. Consequently, every state functional that is non-increasing under the corresponding intermediate maps is non-increasing in homogeneous exterior sectors and non-decreasing in homogeneous interior sectors. The framework therefore applies to broad classes of quantum resources and correlations, including entanglement and occupation-basis coherence monotones, optimized Bell-functional quantities, and contractive-divergence correlation measures. We further numerically evaluate collective coherence based on the quantum Jensen-Shannon divergence (QJSD) in the Garfinkle-Horowitz-Strominger (GHS) dilaton-black-hole spacetime, illustrating the predicted homogeneous monotonicity. The recurring trends are therefore traced to a common channel-ordering structure, while the physical setting determines the parameterization of $q$ and the resource-theoretic monotonicity determines which output-state quantities inherit the order.
summary: This work develops a structural framework for analyzing quantum resources near black hole horizons by modeling the fermionic transformation as two complementary quantum channels: exterior and interior. The key finding is that these two channels exhibit opposite ordering behaviors with respect to a system parameter $q$. This reveals a universal channel-ordering structure responsible for predictable monotonicity in various quantum correlations.
main_problem: To establish whether monotonic trends observed in relativistic quantum information near black holes stem from specific measurement choices or a universal underlying structural principle.
main_result: The exterior and interior fermionic horizon channels exhibit opposite post-processing orders with respect to the channel parameter $q$, leading to predictable monotonicity for various state functionals.
method: Formulating the transformation as complementary quantum channels and analyzing their ordering properties using degradation preorders ($\succeq_{	ext{deg}}$) in both single-mode and multipartite settings.
model_or_system: The analysis is set in relativistic quantum information theory, specifically modeling fermionic modes near black hole horizons (e.g., GHS dilaton spacetime). The core mathematical tool is the effective single-mode fermionic horizon transformation parameterized by $q$.
key_observables: Entanglement, occupation-basis coherence monotones, optimized Bell-functional quantities, and collective coherence based on Quantum Jensen-Shannon divergence (QJSD).
important_parameters: The relativistic channel parameter $q$, which governs the relative weighting between accessible (exterior) and inaccessible (interior) quantum sectors.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that the relevant mode transformation can be effectively described by a two-level system, allowing for the definition of complementary exterior and interior channels.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but numerical evaluation is performed on collective coherence in the GHS black hole spacetime to illustrate predicted homogeneous monotonicity.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem by noting ambiguity in resource trends. It then derives the complementary exterior and interior channels ($	ext{E}_{	ext{out}}^q$ and $	ext{E}_{	ext{in}}^q$) and establishes their opposite ordering properties as $q$ changes. Finally, it generalizes this to multipartite settings and connects channel ordering directly to state functional monotonicity.
why_interesting: It provides a structural theory for resource flow in curved spacetime, suggesting that the observed monotonic behavior is dictated by the underlying mathematical structure of the horizon channels rather than the specific physical measure used.
